episodes.title: History of the Taiping Rebellion
episodes.description: Journey into one of the bloodiest and most transformative conflicts of 19th-century China and discover the extraordinary history of the Taiping Rebellion. This episode explores the origins, rise, and devastating fall of the Taiping movement, led by Hong Xiuquan, a religious visionary who believed he had a divine mission to establish a new heavenly kingdom in China. Discover how social unrest, poverty, corruption, economic hardship, and religious upheaval helped transform a growing movement into a massive rebellion. Explore the capture of Nanjing and the establishment of the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom, as well as its revolutionary religious beliefs, social reforms, military organization, and attempts to reshape Chinese society. We examine the movement's leaders, internal rivalries, armies, major battles, and its struggle against the Qing government. The episode also examines the enormous human cost of the conflict. Millions of people were affected by warfare, famine, disease, displacement, and destruction as Qing forces, regional armies, and foreign interests became involved in the struggle. Discover the role of figures such as Zeng Guofan, Li Hongzhang, Charles Gordon, and other military and political leaders who helped shape the final stages of the rebellion. We also explore the fall of Nanjing in 1864 and the eventual destruction of the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom. Drawing on Chinese historical records, eyewitness accounts, military documents, missionary writings, and modern scholarship, this episode separates established history from propaganda, legend, and later interpretations. Narrated with a calm, human voice, this immersive journey through 19th-century Chinese history is perfect for history enthusiasts, military history lovers, Chinese history fans, documentary listeners, relaxation, or listening before sleep. Discover the beliefs, battles, leaders, tragedies, and lasting legacy of the Taiping Rebellion.
